[Intro] Yeah, mówię ci – Lśni przed światem jak złota gwiazda, ale za zamkniętymi drzwiami wciąż rośnie mrok.

[Refren] Z aureolą, tak czarujący, tak doskonały, a w jego królestwie tylko ból i chaos trwały. Anioł na scenie, lecz w domu tyran – Aureola, twój blask jest zimny i złamany.

[Zwrotka 1] Hipnotyzuje tłumy, zawsze elegancki w świetle, obiecuje miłość wieczną, lecz to tylko ułuda w świecie. Ale za maską kryje się cień, co wszystko niszczy, cichy dyktator, który każdy płomień gasi. Jego słodkie słowa to trucizna w każdym wersie, a w domu rządzi surowo – w chłodzie, bez serca. Pod migoczącą kurtyną jaskrawego światła, pęka serce w mroku – rozdarte, zapomniane, stracone.

[Refren] Z aureolą, tak czarujący, tak doskonały, a w jego królestwie tylko ból i chaos trwały. Anioł na scenie, lecz w domu tyran – Aureola, twój blask jest zimny i złamany.

[Zwrotka 2] Na oczach ludzi – gwiazda, co rozświetla noc, lecz za zamkniętymi drzwiami rządzi gniew i moc. Udaje anioła, słodkie słowa rzuca w tłum, ale w cieniu w domu jego miłość to grób. Każdy komplement trucizną cicho mnie trawi, gdy prawda tonie w fałszu, co każdy dzień zdobi. Buduje świątynie kłamstw, wiecznie nową twarz, lecz ja łamię te kajdany – moje serce odzyska blask.

metadata.prompt:
On a very high mountain, thin air and morning chill,
A structure like a city shone southward, vast and still.
A man, bronze-bright, with linen cord and reed in hand,
Stood where the wind pressed dust in curls across the land.

The sun struck stone; his measuring reed clicked, firm and true,
Each cubit set, each pace declared what Yahowah drew.
Footfalls echoed on bedrock steps, crisp in the light,
While cloud-shadows slid over ridges left and right.

He measured the wall, thick breadth of six cubits wide,
Its face like chiseled limestone, lime-smell, chalk-dry tide.
The gate on the east rose square with threshold clean,
The hinge-pins cold, the lintel cut with palm leaves green.

Guard-chambers three by three flanked halls of hammered floor,
Their benches smoothed by hands, grain tight, oiled cedar door.
Thin windows latticed light in bands across the dust,
While sand hissed in the gusts that combed the desert crust.

The threshold’s length he called, the jambs he chalked in line,
The sockets whiter than the salt at quarries’ spine.
From sill to ceiling beam, the reed set breadth and span,
The cadence of the cubit marked design to plan.

The outer court lay paved with stones that held the heat,
Thirty chambers faced the square with shaded seat.
Steps murmured under sandals, leather dry and worn,
Small swallows stitched the blue with wings at break of morn.

North gate and south gate mirrored east in measured grace,
Carved palms and budding stems climbed every post in place.
The bronze man tapped the marks; the numbers matched the frame,
The desert wind repeated them like quiet flame.

He crossed the pavement’s glare to inner court’s cool ring,
Its steps rose steeper, railings tight like harp-string string.
The scent of cedar planks breathed resin, warm and light,
While shadows pooled where pillars cooled the noon-day bright.

Before the house, the square lay set, an altar’s site,
Smooth hewn, awaiting fire when seasons call to rite.
He marked its ledge and base, the horns reserved and clean,
Fine dust like sifted flour clung pale and keen.

The porch of the house stood deep, its threshold long,
The side-walls squared the breeze that hummed a steady song.
The doors were double, folding leaves with careful grain,
Their pivot-cups like polished cups that drank no stain.

He measured the nave, long breadth where footsteps slow,
Where light from narrow windows fell in silver flow.
The boards fit tight; no iron showed, yet strength was sure,
Stone joined to timber, line to line, precise and pure.

Beyond, the inner room—set-apart within set-apart
A silence thick as felt enclosed the guarded heart.
The reed declared its perfect span, length matched to breadth,
Cool air held still, as if the walls restrained the breath.

Around the house, three stories rose of side-rooms bound,
Each higher tier a broader ledge around the mound.
Stairways coiled like shells, soft echoes up the turn,
Palm-lattice shadows scrolled the walls where lamps would burn.

The separate place to west lay fenced and clean,
A court where no debris or casual tread was seen.
He marked its length with steady hand, dust dull and gray,
While clouds like fleece rolled shoreward from the far off bay.

He gauged the priests’ chambers north and south of stone,
Where linen dried on lines, where bread and oil were known.
Basins cool as winter streams, drains cut and true,
Smooth plaster tough as river clay the workmen threw.

The pavement’s edge ran straight, a border band of white,
It framed the courts like shoreline frames the inland light.
The reed kept time: a crisp click, pause, then click again,
Like droplets counting cave-ribs in a hidden glen.

He walked the outer bounds, four squares of measured peace,
From corner sun to shadowed gate, exact release.
Wind combed the grass that braved the cracks between the slabs,
Small lizards warmed on thresholds, darting into abs.

Five hundred by five hundred round, enclosure set,
A hedge to separate the common from the net.
No idle tread would cross where service meets the Name,
Stone, timber, linen, bronze aligned without a claim.

We stood while evening cooled the wall with violet shade,
The western sky poured copper light where numbers laid.
From reed to cord, from cord to chalk, the proof ran clear,
Yahowah’s pattern fixed in rock year after year.

So mark the reed, recall the cubit’s steady tone,
Let dust and sun bear witness where His plan was shown.
For when the cloud returns and settles on this height,
These measured courts will welcome Yahowah’s set-apart light.

moviendo máquina,
oliendo aromas indeseables,
tu salida maquinas 
del ciclo que odias.

todos los días.

para atravesar la línea.

y más, y más aumenta tu desprecio.

lo que no es tuyo
y bajar de la máquina.

de vida indeseada,
rutina, que no escogiste..

lograr calcular el motivo
de tu desgracia,
de lo que llamas mala.

pero los demás siempre
tendrán la culpa.

base de los pensamientos,
a llegado el día 
de dejar la máquina y 
cambiarla por la 
quimera truena fuego.

dejándolo retorcido en sus adentros.

que con la soberbia lo has
comido, masticado, escupido
y vuelto a comer.

sueltas de su mente divagando
sin rumbo fijo.

has dejado su mente

sumergiéndola en el muro de la nada.

 su único vestigio en el  universo inmenso
de su mente que permanece latente,
desconectado, concentrado
en un pun

metadata.prompt:
/* Suno, — The musical style dominating the general tagging of the text, that's why I allowed myself to experiment in this direction. It is very sad that it is impossible to work out the parts of the voice separately and the music separately minimally, as well as that there is no division of the musical style into the description of the melody and the performance features for the vocals. The style, as a template of a certain "portrait of the melody/Persona" was expected, but it is essentially just a random mixture of the shortcomings that I described above. Thank you for your understanding and I look forward to development!*/
/* Music is above all, but the song should not be devoid of voice and content. If you liked my experiments, then let me know with your voice! Enjoy listening!*/

[Intro: 8 bars, Adagio; expressive cello and violin lead with gentle piano chords, setting a somber, baroque-inspired atmosphere] [Gm Bb Eb]

[Musical Interlude: 4 bars; strings swell, piano accentuates the mood with light arpeggios] [Gm D F Bb]

[Verse Transition: 4 bars; cello deepens, adding a sense of longing before the next verse] [Eb Bb D Gm]

[Instrumental Break: 6 bars; violin and cello duet, intensifying the reflective atmosphere] [Gm Dm F Eb]

[Outro: 6 bars; piano and strings gently fade, leaving a lasting echo of the main theme] [Gm Bb Dm Eb]

metadata.tags: A eurodance anthem in A minor opens with 8 bars of lush pads and piano stabs, white-noise riser swelling. The verse strips back: analog synth bass, sparse chords, chopped female vocal samples. Pre-chorus introduces bright trance plucks and rapid hi-hats. Chorus erupts with massive detuned saw leads, punchy side-chained bass, uplifting arpeggiated and gated pads. The bridge breaks down to filtered, reverbed vocals with spoken-word FX and a gated snare roll, building tension. Throughout: driving kick, tight claps, stereo delays on lead, emotive echo-laden female vocals.

metadata.tags: Begins with distant didgeridoo drones, bone percussion, and reversed chants, panned for ritual atmosphere. Sub-heavy 808s and throat singing pulse in, joined by rattling chains, shakers, and dark pads. The build spirals with frenetic percussion, animal screeches, glitchy FX, and distorted mantras, peaking in a frenzied climax of layered drums and bass, then dissolving in echo, breath loops, and rumbling reverb. Cinematic, menacing, and hypnotic throughout.

[TITLE: Omina Caelorum] (Omens of the Skies)
[LANGUAGES: Latin, Akkadian, Ancient Greek, Old Church Slavonic]
[GENRE: Ritual Chant | Cosmic Ode | Ancestral Bass]
[MOOD: Mystical | Unnamed | Celestial | Dissonant Wonder]
[BPM: 80]
[VOCALS: Whispered, Sung, Chanted, Layered]
[INSTRUMENTATION: Deep Drums, Echoed Bells, Wind FX, Celestial Choir, Bone Flutes]

[Intro – Whispered English Translation]
Fire flees without a voice
A sign in the sky—neither sought nor held

[Verse 1 – English Translation]
That which writes upon the sky has no name
The star passed above like a river through stone

[Chorus – English Translation]
The sky is split, and order passes
It stays not, yet it warns

[Bridge – English Translation]
She comes burning, she does not stay
She sees not, speaks not—only scatters

[Verse 2 – English Translation]
A fire in the sky—a cross without a name
It comes, it breaks, it does not return

[Chorus – English Translation, Repeated]
A fugitive path, no trail left behind
A burning without record

[Outro – English Translation]
In the ancient sky, it carved a path
And no trace remained—silence holds it

metadata.tags: Begin with a surreal, atmospheric jazz intro—upright bass bouncing off gentle brushwork, Rhodes piano casting fractured, echoing chords. Angular woodwinds enter, swirling in odd meters. The verses ride on a lopsided, pulsing groove—modular synths refract notes, tempos shifting unpredictably. Short instrumental fills warp through spectral effects, mimicking time distortion. The chorus erupts: brass stabs, rumbling sub-bass, microtonal guitar slides, while a theremin sings overhead. Brief breakdowns dissolve into near silence, only to be overtaken by chaotic polyrhythms and a cathartic, dissonant swell. The outro fades with distance—glitchy piano, brushed cymbals, and a single, looping bassline, fading into low, cosmic noise.
metadata.prompt:
Norwegian salmon fold into quantum eel migrations, writhing upstream through fjords of time's fractured amber. Eggs whipped into nebulae— their yolks screaming with the collapse of false vacuums, omelette curdling into a nursery of white dwarf stillbirths. Beetroots spiral, flesh demanding the surrender of entropy's last breaths, their concentric wounds staining event horizons. I claim this.

Avocado toast smeared with ontological collapse, void-salted. A side of gravitational syrup pooling into event horizons where the crumbs fall. Hollandaise curdling with the weight of existence—spooned over truths too soft to hold their shape. Mimosa fizzing with philosophers' carbonated tears, decanted from the joke's eventide. *Two seats by the accretion disc, please.* They recognize my silhouette here—the one carved by all that slips beyond the pit's eventless hunger.

I claim this.

(igy nem szökik rá hirtelen az éj)

s mig kis szive nagyon szorongva dobban,
tán ő se tudja, mit is kiván jobban,
a mesét-e, vagy azt, hogy ott legyél:
igy kérünk: Ülj le közénk és mesélj.
Mondd el, mit szoktál, bár mi nem feledjük,
mesélj arról, hogy itt vagy velünk együtt
s együtt vagyunk veled mindannyian,
kinek emberhez méltó gondja van.

Te jól tudod, a költő sose lódit:
az igazat mondd, ne csak a valódit,
a fényt, amelytől világlik agyunk,
hisz egymás nélkül sötétben vagyunk.
Ahogy Hans Castorp madame Chauchat testén,
hadd lássunk át magunkon itt ez estén.
Párnás szavadon át nem üt a zaj –
mesélj arról, mi a szép, mi a baj,
emelvén szivünk a gyásztól a vágyig.
Most temettük el szegény Kosztolányit
s az emberségen, mint rajta a rák,
nem egy szörny-állam iszonyata rág
s mi borzadozva kérdezzük, mi lesz még,
honnan uszulnak ránk uj ordas eszmék,
fő-e uj méreg, mely közénk hatol –
meddig lesz hely, hol fölolvashatol?…
Arról van szó, ha te szólsz, ne lohadjunk,
de mi férfiak férfiak maradjunk
és nők a nők – szabadok, kedvesek
– s mind ember, mert az egyre kevesebb…
Foglalj helyet. Kezdd el a mesét szépen.
Mi hallgatunk és lesz, aki csak éppen
néz téged, mert örül, hogy lát ma itt
fehérek közt egy európait.

O Captain! my Captain! our fearful trip is done,
The ship has weather’d every rack, the prize we sought is won,
The port is near, the bells I hear, the people all exulting,
While follow eyes the steady keel, the vessel grim and daring;
                         But O heart! heart! heart!
                            O the bleeding drops of red,
                               Where on the deck my Captain lies,
                                  Fallen cold and dead.

O Captain! my Captain! rise up and hear the bells;
Rise up—for you the flag is flung—for you the bugle trills,
For you bouquets and ribbon’d wreaths—for you the shores a-crowding,
For you they call, the swaying mass, their eager faces turning;
                         Here Captain! dear father!
                            This arm beneath your head!
                               It is some dream that on the deck,
                                 You’ve fallen cold and dead.

My Captain does not answer, his lips are pale and still,
My father does not feel my arm, he has no pulse nor will,
The ship is anchor’d safe and sound, its voyage closed and done,
From fearful trip the victor ship comes in with object won;
                         Exult O shores, and ring O bells!

                            But I with mournful tread,
                               Walk the deck my Captain lies,
                                  Fallen cold and dead.

metadata.prompt:
Нажмите кнопку включения питания на вашем системнике, и спустя несколько секунд вы увидите окно входа в систему.

Посмею предположить, что каждого интересовало хоть когда-либо то, что происходит за занавесом заставок и загрузочных экранов с момента включения питания компьютера к моменту, когда предлагается войти в систему.

Я предлагаю вам познакомиться со следующими уровнями типичной загрузки Linux:

1. BIOS

BIOS отвечает за базовый ввод/вывод данных с устройств/на устройства.
Делает некоторые проверки целостности устройств. К тому же, за тестирование работоспособности электроники отвечает POST (Power-on self-test, он же «тест на адекватность себя самого», выполняющийся как этап пре-загрузки), который управляется BIOS
Ищет, загружает и выполняет программу-загрузчик ОС
Берет загрузчик из флопика, сидюка или жесткого диска. Во время загрузки BIOS'а вы можете нажать на кнопку (обычно это F12 или F2 или Del, зависит от платформы), если вам требуется внести некоторые изменения касательно настройки железа.
Как только загрузчик был обнаружен и загружен в память, BIOS передает управление ему.
Короче говоря, BIOS загружает и выполняет загрузочную запись (MBR).


2. MBR

MBR — это главная загрузочная запись, хранящаяся на жестком диске
Она размещена в 1-м секторе загрузочного диска, например /dev/hda или /dev/sda
MBR занимает меньше, чем 512 байтов. Она состоит из трех компонентов: 1) главная загрузочная информация, «живущая» в первых 446 байтах; 2) информация о таблице разделов — в следующих 64 байтах; 3) и последние 2 байта нужны для проверки корректности mbr.
Она содержит информацию о GRUB'е (или LILO).
Простыми словами — MBR загружает и выполняет загрузчик GRUB.

3. GRUB

GRUB — Grand Unified Bootloader.
Если в вашей системе установлено более, чем одно ядро, у вас есть возможность выбирать, которое из них должен выполняться
GRUB отображает красивую анимацию plymouth заставку, и, подождав несколько секунд интерактивного воздействия пользователя, если он не нажал ни одной клавиши, он загружает ядро, установленное по умолчанию в файле конфигурации grub.
GRUB понимает, что такое файловая система (древние загрузчики Linux'а, например, LILO этого не понимают).
Конфигурационный файл Grub обычно лежит по пути /boot/grub/grub.conf (так же /etc/grub.conf может быть символьной ссылкой на него). В качестве примечания к информации выше, конфигурационный файл содержит путь к ядру и образу initrd

4. Ядро или Kernel

Ядро монтирует файловую систему в соответствии с настройкой «root=» в фале grub.conf
Выполняет программу /sbin/init
Поскольку init — это первый процесс, запущенный ядром Linux, поэтому она имеет идентификатор процесса (PID) №1. Можете выполнить «ps -ef | grep init» и убедиться в этом.
initrd — это Initial RAM Disk, он же временный диск в оперативной памяти
initrd используется самим ядром в качестве временной корневой файловой системы, пока kernel не загрузится в реальную примонтированную файловую систему. Этот временный диск также содержит необходимые для загрузки драйверы, позволяющие получить доступ к разделам дисков и другому оборудованию

5. Init

Смотрит в файл /etc/inittab для того, чтобы определить уровень выполнения (run level).
Есть следующие уровни выполнения:
0 – прервать выполнение
1 – Однопользовательский режим, так называемый «Single user mode», или иными словами, консоль восстановления
2 – Многопользовательский режим без поддержки NFS
3 – Полноценный многопользовательский режим
4 – не используется
5 – X11
6 – перезагрузка
Init определяет уровень выполнения по умолчанию исходя из /etc/inittab и использует его для загрузки всех необходимых программ.
Выполните «grep initdefault /etc/inittab»

6. Уровень выполнения программ (Runlevel)

Когда Линукс выполняет свою загрузку, вы можете наблюдать загрузку различных служб. К примеру, это могут быть сообщения типа «starting Postfix … OK» (запускается Postfix). Эти службы — и называются программами уровня выполнения, выполняемые из директории, которая соответствует нужному уровню выполнения.
Исходя из настроек по умолчанию, система будет выполнять файлы в соответствии с нижеприведенными директориями.
Выполнение уровня 0 – /etc/rc.d/rc0.d/
Выполнение уровня 1 – /etc/rc.d/rc1.d/
Выполнение уровня 2 – /etc/rc.d/rc2.d/
Выполнение уровня 3 – /etc/rc.d/rc3.d/
Выполнение уровня 4 – /etc/rc.d/rc4.d/
Выполнение уровня 5 – /etc/rc.d/rc5.d/
Выполнение уровня 6 – /etc/rc.d/rc6.d/
Но имейте ввиду, что еще в каталоге /etc могут быть символические ссылки. Например, /etc/rc0.d залинкован на /etc/rc.d/rc0.d.
В каталогах /etc/rc.d/rc*.d/ вы можете увидеть список программ, имя которых начинается из букв S и K.
Программы, начинающиеся на S используются для запуска. S, потому что startup.
Программы, которые начинаются с литеры K используются — правильно — для завершения работы. K, потому что kill.
Еще есть номера рядом с буквами S и K в именах программ. 

Программы, начинающиеся на S используются для запуска. S, потому что startup.
Программы, которые начинаются с литеры K используются — правильно — для завершения работы. K, потому что kill.
Еще есть номера рядом с буквами S и K в именах программ. Эти номера используются для определения порядка запуска этих программ.
К примеру, S12syslog предназначен для запуска демона syslog, его порядковый номер 12. S80sendmail — для запуска демона sendmail, имеющего порядковый номер 80. Таким образом, программа syslog будет запущена перед sendmail.


Вот и все. Возможно, некоторым из вас это не ново и особого интереса не было при чтении статью, поскольку она более ориентирована на начально-средний уровень знакомства з Линуксом.
В таком случае могу лишь сказать, что «повторение — мать учения» (с).

Welcome to nowhere,

[Chorus] 
welcome to nowhere, headlights on, Living like the punchline of a half-written song. We’re stuck on repeat, stuck on repeat, stuck But somehow all the stars line up (We’re stuck on repeat, stuck on repeat, stuck) (But somehow all the stars line up)

[Verse 2] 
We snuck onto rooftops, just to kill time, Counting satellite trails and graffiti signs. You said, “Do you think we’ll remember this night?” I said, “If we don’t, it’s probably right.”
We played dumb games on a gameboy you found, The beeps and your silence both equally loud. But then you paused, looked up, and said, "Isn’t it wild how this feels like the end?"

Conceito: Uma versão brutal e distorcida da clássica cantiga de roda infantil, "Alecrim Dourado", transformada em um hino de morte e destruição.
Atmosfera: Sombria, caótica, com elementos góticos e macabros.
Emoções: Raiva, ódio, desespero, niilismo.
Imagens: Um jardim abandonado e sombrio, com flores mortas e terra rachada. Criaturas grotescas e retorcidas se alimentando de carne putrefata.
Sons: Riff de guitarra distorcida, blast beats frenéticos, vocais guturais profundos, efeitos sonoros de chuva e trovões.
Prompt Detalhado:
Música: Crie uma música de death metal técnico e agressivo, com riffs complexos e mudanças de tempo constantes. A melodia deve ser sombria e dissonante, contrastando com a melodia infantil original.
Letra: Adapte a letra da cantiga de roda para um contexto macabro e violento. Utilize metáforas e imagens chocantes para transmitir a atmosfera de morte e destruição. Explore temas como a decadência, a solidão e a perda da inocência.
Estrutura: A música deve começar com uma introdução lenta e atmosférica, com sons de chuva e trovões. Em seguida, a música deve explodir em um caos frenético, com riffs pesados e blast beats implacáveis. Um breakdown lento e pesado pode ser usado para descrever a decomposição da natureza.
Elementos Sonoros:
 * Sons de natureza: Utilize sons de chuva, trovões e vento para criar uma atmosfera sombria e opressiva.
 * Efeitos de distorção: Crie um som pesado e agressivo, contrastando com a melodia infantil original.
 * Vocais guturais: Utilize vocais profundos e guturais para transmitir a raiva e o ódio.
Exemplo de trecho da letra adaptada:
> "Alecrim dourado, nasceu do campo sem ser semeado
> Agora apodrece, em um jardim de pesadelo
> Raízes retorcidas, sugando a vida da terra
> Flores mortas, um altar para a guerra"
> 
Ideias adicionais:
 * Elementos góticos: Utilize elementos góticos como castelos abandonados, cemitérios e criaturas sobrenaturais.
 * Ritual satânico: A letra pode sugerir que a cantiga de roda é parte de um ritual satânico.
 * Distorção da melodia infantil: Utilize a melodia original da cantiga de roda, mas distorcida e corrompida, para criar um efeito dissonante e perturbador.
Título Sugerido: "Alecrim Negro" ou "Jardim da Morte"
Bandas de referência: Cannibal Corpse, Dying Fetus, Carcass, Morbid Angel, Suffocation, Napalm Death.

Canção Atual:
•	Toda a música deve ser somente em estúdio [recinto apropriado e equipado para realização de gravação sonora]. 
•	Não deve haver comentários falados fora da letra, dos vocais, a não ser quando o comando indicar recitações da letra.
•	Instrumentos, produção, masterização e outros, devem ser do tempo presente.
•	O sentimento de cada acorde deve estar de acordo com a letra cantada no momento.
•	A cadência autêntica perfeita deve ter 75% de prioridade, a cadência plagal, 25%, e a cadência enganosa, quando a parte da letra exigir.
•	A melodia deve ter cadência autêntica perfeita, forte e conclusiva.
•	Os vocais devem ser harmoniosos, melódicos e limpos, com duetos, melismas, voz de cabeça forte em registros agudos, ressonância nasal para clareza e assobios melódicos.
•	Os vocais devem ter pronúncia, enunciação e dicção, claras.
•	A melodia deve ter 
•	Tonalidade: menor natural, com cadência (progressão) autêntica perfeita (I-VI-VII-I).
•	Idioma dos vocais: inglês americano, moderno e perfeito.
•	Gênero e estilo: rock, power ballad.
•	Use 3 guitarras elétricas, 2 para a harmonia e 1 para o ritmo. 
•	Use 2 guitarras gêmeas (em terça).
•	As introduções musicais devem conter guitarras elétricas sem distorção.
•	Bateria, baixo e guitarras, com linhas galopantes.
•	A bateria deve combinar uma técnica com um único pedal de notas rápidas e com pedal duplo. 
•	O estilo vocal de alcance operístico, com um timbre poderoso e agudo, "Air Raid Siren" (Sirene de Ataque Aéreo). Utilize técnicas para alongar a voz e mantê-la clara e forte. O timbre deve ser potente e "aberto", o que é contrastante com timbres mais escuros usados no rock. Nas técnicas de projeção vocal, utilize um palato alto e a manipulação da língua, para clarear a voz e atingir os agudos de forma consistente. 

Princípios:
1.	Origem divina – Todo dom musical vem de Deus e serve ao Seu propósito, mesmo por meio de artistas não regenerados (Tiago 1:17; Êxodo 31:2–4).
2.	Clareza e ordem – A música deve ser inteligível, bem estruturada e coerente com a mensagem (1 Coríntios 14:8, 14:40).
3.	Expressão emocional santa – Melodia, ritmo e dinâmica devem refletir emoções verdadeiras, guiadas pela Escritura (1 Samuel 16:23; Eclesiastes 3:1).
4.	Afinação e excelência – Sons desafinados ou mal executados são rejeitados por Deus (Amós 5:23); a excelência glorifica a Ele.
5.	Unidade e função – Cada voz e instrumento deve cumprir um papel específico, como membros de um só corpo (1 Coríntios 12:17–18).
6.	Letra bíblica – As letras devem ensinar, exortar e louvar com fidelidade à Palavra (Colossenses 3:16).
7.	Vocal ungido – Técnicas como respiração, articulação, tom e projeção são dons espirituais e devem servir à proclamação (Gênesis 2:7; Salmo 29:9).
8.	Melodia profética – A melodia proclama a verdade, conduz à adoração e ensina a doutrina com beleza e reverência (Salmo 96:1; João 4:24).
9.	Liturgia e narrativa – A música deve seguir o arco bíblico de criação, queda e redenção, conduzindo o ouvinte pelo evangelho (Gênesis 1:1; Apocalipse 21:5).
10.	Unção e transformação – A música redentora consola, confronta, ensina e molda culturas, pois carrega o poder da Palavra viva (2 Crônicas 5:13; Romanos 12:2).

a song in English. In the small town of Maplewood, where everyone knew everyone else’s business, there was a curious misunderstanding brewing at St. Agatha’s Church. Marianne—a lively, affectionate woman with a flair for drama—was utterly convinced that Robert, the quiet, reserved churchgoer, was hopelessly in love with her. According to Marianne’s interpretation, every polite nod, every fleeting glance, and even that one accidental meeting of eyes during the hymn were all secret declarations of passion.

Robert, however, was as straightforward as they came. A man of strict routines and steadfast manners, he was more intent on keeping his eyes fixed on the altar than on any potential romantic interest. Due to a rather old-fashioned church rule (or so he claimed) that “diverted gazes lead to heavenly distractions,” he made sure his sight remained dutifully on his prayer book—except for the rare, accidental moments when his eyes met Marianne’s. And those, he would later insist with a polite smile, were pure coincidences!

Marianne’s belief in Robert’s secret adoration grew with every service. She was so convinced of his hidden feelings that she often boasted to anyone who'd listen, “I can practically see him losing his mind over me! The way he blushes when our eyes meet—it’s divine madness!” Determined to clarify the situation and, in her own way, help Robert come to terms with his “love,” she concocted a plan involving her quick-witted niece, Elise.

One sunny Sunday after the morning service, Marianne cornered Robert near the flower-bedecked church steps. With a twinkle in her eye, she announced, “Robert, my dear—your secret love for me is written all over you! Why don’t you just admit it?” Before Robert could muster an explanation, Elise, who had been tagging along, piped up in a matter-of-fact tone, “Uncle Robert, you’re a busy man with your Bible studies and choir practice—plus, you once told me you’d never even minded looking around in church because there’s nothing for you to see except the Lord’s grace!”

The comment left the gathered parishioners snickering. Robert looked as if he’d been caught in a blizzard of confusion. “I—I assure you, Mrs. Marianne, and you, Elise—I am absolutely not in love,” he stammered. “If anything, I’m just following the rules. I’m allowed to glance at the altar—nothing more.”

Marianne’s eyes widened in disbelief, yet she remained unshaken. “Oh, Robert, your ‘not in love’ is just a front! I see it in your gentle smile and those accidental glances during the sermon!” she argued, half-whispering conspiratorially.

Robert sighed quietly. He could understand Marianne’s passion, but he had no personal stake in a romantic entanglement with her. “Marianne, I value you as a dear friend and a fellow believer,” he said kindly. “But my heart is not, nor will it ever be, a chaotic mess of unspoken infatuation. I’m here for the love of God.”

Despite his earnest assurances and Elise’s candid confirmation, Marianne continued to interpret every gesture as a secret sign of undying affection. In the weeks that followed, the church buzzed with whispers about how Marianne was “driving Robert crazy” with her persistent declarations. Every time their eyes met—whether over the hymn book or as Robert dutifully passed by the bell tower—Marianne felt a spark of triumph. To her, it was proof of an unspoken romance; to Robert, it was merely an incidental collision of sightlines in a place of worship.

In time, even as the humorous rumor grew in eccentricity among the townsfolk, Robert gently maintained the boundaries. He continued his quiet, careful existence, and though Marianne’s persistent antics became the subject of many a raised eyebrow and chuckle (at church socials and community picnics alike), he remained the same steadfast man.

And so, in Maplewood, the saga of Marianne’s unwavering—and entirely misplaced—belief in Robert’s love became a beloved anecdote. It served as a lighthearted reminder that sometimes perceptions, no matter how fervently held, can stray far from the truth. **Step-by-Step Explanation for Creating "Feel The Energy":**

**1. Project Setup & Tempo/Key Alignment**  
- Set DAW to **128 BPM** and key to **A Minor**.  
- Create a click track or metronome reference for timing.  

**2. Intro (8 Bars)**  
- **Drums**: Layer a punchy kick (e.g., Splice “Festival_Kick_128”) with off-beat hi-hats (16th notes). Apply a low-pass filter to the hats.  
- **Vocals**: Process the spoken line (“The night is calling…”) with **deep reverb** (Valhalla VintageVerb) and a **low-pass filter** (cutoff ~1 kHz).  
- **FX**: Add white noise sweeps (output by Output) rising every 2 bars. Use a snare roll (starting at bar 6) with increasing speed. Automate filter cutoff on the noise sweep to open up toward the verse.  

**3. Verse (16 Bars)**  
- **Melody**: Program a plucked arp (Serum or Nexus “Pluck Legends”) with chords **Am-G-F-G** (A minor, G major, F major, G major). Use staccato notes for rhythm.  
- **Vocals**: Record or sample the verse lyrics (“Lost in the sound…”). Apply **light reverb** (FabFilter Pro-R) and sidechain to the kick (LFOTool or ShaperBox).  
- **Bass**: Introduce a mid-bass (Serum “Grit Bass”) swelling in with a slow LFO on the volume. Layer a sub-bass (Sine wave, 808-style) sidechained to the kick.  

**4. Build-Up (8 Bars)**  
- **Drums**: Add snare rolls (XLN Audio Addictive Drums) accelerating every bar. Layer risers (KSHMR Essentials Risers).  
- **Vocals**: Chop “Higher, higher, feel the fire!” into 1/16th notes. Apply **delay** (EchoBoy) and automate the delay feedback to increase.  
- **Synths**: Automate pitch bends on a lead synth (rising +12 semitones over 8 bars).  

**5. Drop (16 Bars)**  
- **Lead Synth**: Stack 3 detuned supersaws (Serum, unison = 8, detune = 12%). Play melody **E5-E5-D5-C5** in triplet rhythm. Sidechain to kick.  
- **Bass**: Layer a distorted mid-bass (CamelCrusher) with a sub-bass (A0-C1).  
- **Vocals**: Process “FEEL THE ENERGY” with distortion (Decapitator) and layer 3x (main, octave up, octave down). Add chopped “Tonight!” echoes panned left/right.  

**6. Breakdown (16 Bars)**  
- **Pads**: Use a lush pad (Omnisphere “Heavenly Pads”) with a high-pass filter (cutoff rising from 200 Hz to 1 kHz).  
- **Piano**: Add a soft electric piano (Keyscape “Dreamy EP”) playing Am-G-F-G in half-time.  
- **Vocals**: Apply **stereo delay** (H-Delay) and reverb to the ethereal vocal (“We ride the waves…”).  

**7. Second Build-Up & Drop**  
- **Variation**: Add a vocoder (Vocals → Ableton Vocoder) to the build-up chant. Include an arpeggiated pluck (Arturia Pigments) in the drop for rhythmic contrast.  

**8. Outro (8 Bars)**  
- **Atmosphere**: Reverse the final riser and fade out. Use a granular synth (Output Portal) on the vocal chop “We ride the soundwaves…” for texture.  

**9. Mixing**  
- **Sidechain**: Route all synths/bass to a compressor (Kick → Sidechain input, ratio 4:1, fast attack/release).  
- **EQ**: Carve space for kick/bass (cut <100 Hz on non-bass elements). Boost supersaw highs at 10 kHz for sparkle.  

**10. Mastering**  
- **Chain**: EQ (cut mud at 250 Hz) → Multiband compression (glue lows) → Limiter (FabFilter Pro-L 2, +5 dB gain).

meta.prompt:
Here’s my story. Can you turn this into something light acoustic? And have a woman sing it.

Part 1: 22 years ago, I opened the blinds to my childhood bedroom window. I performed an annual ritual that began when I was small. I searched the inky darkness of the midnight sky for the biggest star I could find. I was convinced when I was younger that this was the star that ancient men followed looking for the King who was to come. 

My reasons that night at 20 were the same as when I was 9. I was searching for that same King. Some sign that it was all true. And that He knew and cared who I was. 

But that night, something was different. The scars and wounds I carried with me cried out in pain for healing, desperate for more. Desperate for more than a sign. Desperate for a relationship with the God who created the universe. 

Just 9 days before, I’d attempted to take my own life to no avail. 8 days before, a friend promised me that this God, this one who knit galaxies, protons, atoms, and time itself  together, wanted to know me and to be known by me. Yet, I wasn’t certain. 

I questioned His care for me after years of sustained trauma, after years of being told how unwanted I was. Yet there was still a tiny spark of hope in me that it might all be true. And so I opened the blinds that night, searching out eternity. 

There it was, the largest star in the sky. And suddenly there He was. Not in the star. But washing over me with the truth of who He is. The truth of who He’d made me to be. And that I was so wanted by Him. So loved. 

I have no earthly explanation for what happened to me Christmas Eve night of 2001. It was completely out of character for me to be filled with anything but a raging anger and hopelessness until that moment.

And yet in that moment, for the first time in my life, I was filled with joy, a confidence that God was with me, and a peace that I’d never before experienced. 

I sobbed out of joy. God’s grace had crashed over me like a tidal wave. 

Sometimes I look back and I’m grieved that I still wander. That I forget the God who loves me. I look at 22 years and think I should be farther along in my journey towards looking like Jesus. But then He speaks and reminds me that He who began a good work in me will carry it on to completion in Christ Jesus. 

This is what Christmas is. Not the toys. Not the unrelenting pressure of the parties and gatherings and busyness. Not even a perfect family gathering with just the right photos. 

No. It’s about birth. Both on a cosmic scale and on the minute scale of our hearts. Jesus was born as a tiny, bawling infant holding the future of each one of us in his tiny fingers. Over time, He grew into the one who would conquer death. 

On Christmas Eve, 2001, I experienced birth as well. A small but resilient seed was planted in my heart and through drought, flood, and scorching sun, it’s grown into a small tree, that often needs considerable pruning. I am not who I will be, but I am not who I was. And this is only possible by the miraculous and yet tender care of God, laying each step for me to find Him. 

And friend, I look to you and ask, who or what are you looking for? What is the deep cry of your heart? 

I can tell you what His is. He desperately desires to know you and be known by you. He has set eternity in your heart to find Him. Look at Him. #christmas #star

A sigma male on the other hand, is something slightly different. He is the antithesis of the alpha male archetype and in a way, also their biggest rivals, because unlike the alpha and by extension, a chad; who strives to become what I mentioned in the previous paragraph because that is what he believes is what ladies actually look for in a perfect man, a sigma male doesn't care about these stereotypes and will actively try to prove the alphas how wrong they are in what they believe, by still getting the girl just by being themselves and doing little to no extra effort.

That being said, unlike an alpha male, getting laid and by extension, getting laid and having a harem of the most attractive women is least of their concern. A sigma couldn’t really care less and doesn’t prioritize women on his agenda, but instead, chooses to better himself. A sigma will look for a woman who'll become a good wife and a good mother to his future children — not a trophy and a baddie he can show off to his other rich friends, which is something the chad may do. As I said, the sigma male couldn't care less what others think of him and how others see him as long as he himself is content with what he's doing.
Furthermore, a sigma male doesn’t like to lead or be labeled as a leader either, and yet, people ironically look towards them to be their leaders. A sigma male instead, defies the norms and instead chooses his own path and road to success, usually preferring to go it alone, which is another trait that’s opposite to the alpha male who loves to be the leader of his pack and wants people to look up to him. An alpha male/chad usually wants to be looked up at for guidance and thinks of himself as a source of wisdom and power for all the betas under him. He will purposely paint himself as the hero of the story because he thinks that's what he needs to be seen as the best version of himself, yet if done incorrectly, they usually come off as tryhard and straight up a**holes who do it for clout.
So why don’t they get along, and why does it look like the chads and the sigmas straight up hate each other? It’s the sigma's mysterious and aloof nature that usually attracts women to him, because unlike the alpha, who actually looks like he's trying to impress the girl, a sigma will just be himself and not reveal much about him, which leaves a lot to be discovered about him, and makes women want to get to know them more. more. Here's a real life example of a chad and a sigma;

Suppose you're a woman out at the bar one Saturday night. You want to let loose, have some fun and maybe, just maybe, get lucky. As you wait there at the bar, waiting for the bartender to make you your drink, you catch the eye of an attractive guy who's been staring at you from across the room for a while now. He's attractive and looks like he puts extra care into his looks. You smile back, and he walks over to you and introduces himself. You guys exchange numbers and you're starting to hit it off really well. You learn a lot about him; you learn that he's the CEO of some big corporation with over a hundred or so employees working under him. He tells you about his Lamborghini, his mansion, his holiday home in the Bahamas, and his yacht where he threw this extravagant birthday party last month for his best friend. You're clearly impressed by all his achievements. THAT is the alpha male.

meta.prompt:
Storm & Memory – Fantasie-Impromptu in C# Minor (Op. posth. 66)
In the spirit of “a stormed soul remembering light.” Stylistically: A virtuosic blend of Romantic urgency and lyrical tenderness. Tempo: ♩ = 84–88 (outer), ♩ = 60–66 (middle).
I. PRELUDE – “The Unstoppable Current” (Bars 1–4)

Texture: Immediate, driving.

    RH: Cascading sixteenth notes—restless, wave-like energy. Each figure surges forward with a liquid intensity.

    LH: Sturdy triplet pulse—like footsteps running downhill, steady but emotionally charged.

    Pedal: Subtle, just enough to connect phrases; avoid smearing.

    Mood: Tension already in full bloom. We're dropped straight into motion — no hesitation.

II. A-THEME – “The Storm That Lives Within” (Bars 5–27)

Character: Urgent, impassioned.

    RH: Continues the moto perpetuo. Lines should sing through the rapid texture—shape every peak and valley.

    LH: Pulses in broken chords, grounding the chaos above. Emphasize harmonic shifts to keep the forward momentum meaningful.

    Expression: Inner fire. Use rubato in phrase endings, brief ritards into climaxes.

    Dynamics: Swell with intensity—don’t flatten it to mechanical. It’s a human storm.

III. TRANSITION – “Fracture” (Bars 28–35)

Mood: The energy frays.

    Subtle deceleration and harmonic shifts hint at vulnerability.

    Introduce ritardando and slight a piacere freedom as RH begins to open up and descend.

IV. B-THEME – “The Memory of Calm” (Bars 36–55)

Key: D♭ Major (enharmonic warmth)
Character: Tender, dreamlike, almost sacred.

    RH: Lyrical cantabile melody, almost like a sung aria. Use soft legato touch, with slight agogic stress on emotional notes (especially sighing motifs and appoggiaturas).

    LH: Arpeggiated support—flowing and unobtrusive. Slight inner voice coloring helps illuminate harmonies.

    Tempo: Freely expressive (molto rubato), with heart-led breathing.

    Ornamentation: Grace-notes and sighs act like echoes from the storm — reminders of fragility.

    Dynamic arc: Starts p, builds to a warm mf, then subsides. Emotional swell without overstatement.

V. RE-ENTRY – “A Flicker, Then Flame” (Bars 56–69)

Transition back: RH begins trembling runs again, but with hesitation.

    The storm reawakens — like a memory you can’t quite bury.

    Dynamics: From mezzo-piano to full forte return.

    Feel: A sense of “reliving,” but now with more awareness.

VI. A-THEME RETURN – “The Echoing Storm” (Bars 70–81)

Same material as before, but slightly more controlled—like riding the storm rather than being thrown by it.

    Push tempo where it wants to go.

    Optional rubato in the second pass can emphasize emotional clarity.

    Climax is more internalized, like strength from survival.

VII. CODA – “The Breath Before Silence” (Bars 82–Final)

Texture: Tightens; intensity concentrates.

    RH: Still racing, but now there are cracks—pauses, silences, sudden drops.

    LH grows more percussive, insistent.

    Final bars: Sudden decrescendo, descent into single, bare notes.

    Ending chord: C# minor – pure, solitary. Held gently.

    Optional: Let final resonance linger like the storm’s aftertaste in memory.

Overall Emotional Arc:

    "From breathless unrest to intimate memory and back—this is the sound of a heart that refuses to forget, and a storm that insists on being heard."
